<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. VII.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>AFter these things, Jesus walked in Galilee <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">After the third <ns0:hi>Passover,</ns0:hi> which happened after our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour had entred upon his Publick Ministry, of which we read, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.1. and all those things which we read of, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5, & 6. done by our Saviour, both at the Feast at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem, Chap.</ns0:hi> 5. and after he went into <ns0:hi>Galilee, Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.1. and had made that Excellent Discourse, of which we had a large account, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6. Jesus continued still to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verse in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> where he was,</ns0:note>: for he would not walk in Jewry <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">for he would not go into <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> nor converse there,</ns0:note>, because the Jews sought to kill him <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">because the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> for the causes mentioned, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.18. <ns0:hi>sought to kill him</ns0:hi>: They had two things (as appeareth from thence) against him. 1. His <ns0:hi>violation of the Sabbath</ns0:hi> (as they thought) by healing him that lay at the Pool of <ns0:hi>Bethesda.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>His making him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self equal with the Father.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:343" />2 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 23.33, 34.</ns0:note> Now the Jews feast of tabernacles was at hand <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>The Feast of Tabernacles</ns0:hi> was a Feast which God or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dained the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> to keep <ns0:hi>the fifteeenth day of the seventh month</ns0:hi> (which some make to answer our <ns0:hi>September,</ns0:hi> others our <ns0:hi>October) Lev.</ns0:hi> 23.34, 39. <ns0:hi>after they had gathered in the Fruits of the Land.</ns0:hi> It was to be kept seven days, the first and last of which days were to be kept as Sabbaths; they were all the seven days to dwell in <ns0:hi>Tents</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Booths,</ns0:hi> in remembrance of the forty years they so dwelt in the Wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derness, passing from <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> as we read there, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 43. Now this <ns0:hi>Festival</ns0:hi> was near at hand; so as we must understand the things following to have happened about the <ns0:hi>September</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>October</ns0:hi> before Christs Suffering, which was at the next <ns0:hi>Passover</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that is, the <ns0:hi>March</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>April</ns0:hi> fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowing, as we count the Months.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 3.31. Acts 1.14.</ns0:note> His brethren <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">His Friends and Kindred; see the Notes on <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 12.47, 48.</ns0:note> therefore said unto him, De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />part hence, and go into Judea, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Either such as did believe in him, or such as did not believe; for <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5. all of them did not believe in him, would have him leave <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> which was the far more ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scure and ignoble part of the Countrey; and go into <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> which was the more nob<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e and famous Province; that those who in that Province followed him, might also see the Miracles which he wrought.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 For <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> no man <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> doeth any thing in secret, and he himself seeketh to be known open<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The things which thou doest, thou doest out of a de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sire by them to be made known, and to spread thy own Fame and Glory. For this <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> is not a proper place, because it is an obscure part in the Countrey. The Phrase which we Translate, to be <ns0:hi>made known,</ns0:hi> is in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. The usage of it here seemeth to be something different from the use of it in other places of Holy Writ. It sometimes signifies <ns0:hi>confidence</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>security</ns0:hi>; and we Translate it boldness, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 13.46. and 26.26. and 28.31. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.20. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 3.6. and 10.19. But this cannot be the sense of this Text; for it were no sense to read it, <ns0:hi>seeketh to be known boldly, confidently,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>securely</ns0:hi>: Sometimes we Translate it <ns0:hi>openly,</ns0:hi> as in this Text; and <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.54. and <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 2.15. It sometimes signifieth a <ns0:hi>freedom of speech, Acts</ns0:hi> 2.29. & 4.13. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 7.4. Some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times it signifieth clearness and plainness of speech, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.24. and 11.14. Sometimes it signifieth a speaking in pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lick Meetings, as in <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 8.32. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 18.20. Dr. <ns0:hi>Ham<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mond</ns0:hi> notes, that it also sometimes signifies to <ns0:hi>speak with Authority, Acts</ns0:hi> 4.29, 31. and <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 6.19. Certainly the word in its primary signification, signifieth a <ns0:hi>freedom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>boldness of speech</ns0:hi>; which <ns0:hi>freedom and boldness</ns0:hi> is necessary to him that speaketh openly, and in Publick Meetings; and is advantaged by the Authority which any man hath to speak: Hence in a secondary sense it may signifie both <ns0:hi>to speak with Authority,</ns0:hi> and also <ns0:hi>to speak in Publick Assemblies</ns0:hi>; and this last I take to be here signified. It is (as our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viours Friends tell him) both against Reason, and the ordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nary course of the World, for men desirous of Opportu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nities to speak boldly and freely in Publick Assemblies, to keep themselves in obscure places, where are no such Pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lick Assemblies.</ns0:note>: If thou do these things, shew thy self to the world <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">They therefore advise him, that if in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed he wrought these Miraculous Operations, and were able to produce such Effects, he would not bury up him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self and his Reputation in such an hole as <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> but shew himself to the more noted and Famous part of the World, which was, as to that part of the World, <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> and at the Feast now, where multitudes of the People would be to Celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 3.21.</ns0:note> neither did his brethren believe in him <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Not all his own Friends and Kindred; he came not onely amongst his own Countrey-men, but among his own Relations, and they received him not: Or if they had some Opinion of him, and some little hopes concerning him, yet they did not believe as they ought to have believed. Certainly there cannot be a greater Proof and Demonstra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, that <ns0:hi>Faith is not of our selves,</ns0:hi> nor a thing in our own power; no, not with all the external Aids of Gospel Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine and Arguments, than is in this Text. We cannot imagine but our Lords Brethren were willing enough to have believed in Christ as the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and Saviour of the World (the very Honour of their Family would have so far inclined them.) It is impossible that they, or any others should have had greater external means, aids, and assistances for their Faith, than Christs Preaching amongst them; and confirming his Doctrine by Miraculous Opera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions before them, if now they had a power <ns0:hi>in their own wills,</ns0:hi> to have loo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t upon Christ as the true <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and Saviour of the World; and accordingly to have received and embraced him; what was the matter <ns0:hi>they believed not,</ns0:hi> or as yet at least they believed not in him?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The time of my Death (say some) of my <ns0:hi>manifesta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion to the World</ns0:hi> (say others); but questionless our Saviour intends no more than his time for his going up to this Feast, for we shall read that he did go up afterward; but (saith he) as yet I cannot go up;</ns0:note>
                  <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but your time is alway ready <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">you may go when you please: And this he further openeth, saying,</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 The world cannot hate you <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">By the World, our Saviour plainly understandeth the men of the World; men not Regenerated, Renewed, and Sanctified. These men, saith he, cannot as yet hate you; there was a time afterward when this part of the World hated all the Disciples of Christ, as Christ foretold, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 15.18. but that was after the Doctrine of the Gospel was more Preached, and made known to the World by the Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of the Apostles: And therefore Christ saith (in that place) that it <ns0:hi>hated him before it hated them.</ns0:hi> Christ first published the Doctrine of the Gospel, and so became the first object of the Worlds hatred on that account. These his Brethren were not concerned (that we read of) at this time in the publication of it, nor had any occasion to make themselves known, and odious to the World upon that account; therefore he saith, the <ns0:hi>World</ns0:hi> (the wicked <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> here so called) could not be reasonably imagined to have any spight or malignity to them. But (saith he) me it hateth; that is apparent from what we met with <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.18.</ns0:note>; but me it hateth <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>, because I testifie of it, that the works thereof are evil <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">But this was not for any fault in Christ, but onely for his Preaching the Doctrine of the Gospel, and free Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proving them for the evil of their works, the corruption of their Doctrine, and the Errors of their Life and Conver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Go ye up unto this feast <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Let not my forbearance to go up, hinder your going up according to the Law.</ns0:note>: I go not up yet unto this feast <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I have some particular rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons, why as yet I will not go to be there at the beginning of it.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> for my time is not yet full come <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">I know my time to go, when it will be most safe and proper for me. I shall be there some time during the Feast, but my time is not yet come. I shall not be there at the beginning of it; <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. it appeareth that he came not into the Temple till about the middle of it, which was three or four days after it was began, for it held seven days, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 23.33, 34. Or his time was not come, because he designed to go very privately without any notice taken of his coming; which must have been, if he had at that time gone up with his Kindred and Acquaintance.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 When he had said these words unto them, he abode <ns0:hi>still</ns0:hi> in Galilee <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He let them take their Journey to <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> to the Feast, without him, and himself still abode in <ns0:hi>Galilee.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 ¶ But when his brethren were gone up, then went he also up unto the feast <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">He went up to shew his Obedience to his Fathers Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mands, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 23.17. The Feast of Tabernacles, was the same with the <ns0:hi>Feast of Ingathering in the end of the Year,</ns0:hi> when they had <ns0:hi>gathered their Labours out of the Field,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 23.16. and that was one of those three times (as appears from that Chapter) <ns0:hi>when all the Males in Israel were to appear before the Lord,</ns0:hi> v. 17. Christ be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing born under the Law, sheweth a punctual Obedience to it; and therefore in Obedience to it, he would go up: But his Wisdom <ns0:hi>dwelt with Prudence</ns0:hi>; and therefore</ns0:note>, not openly, but as it were in secret <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">he did not go up <ns0:hi>openly,</ns0:hi> not in any croud of Company, so as a publick notice could be taken of him; but <ns0:hi>secretly,</ns0:hi> to teach us, that we are not so strictly tyed up to <ns0:hi>Ritual Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cepts,</ns0:hi> which concern onely Rites and Circumstances of Worship, that we may not abate them sometimes for the performance of Moral Duties. It was a Moral Duty in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumbent upon our Saviour to preserve himself with what Wisdom and Prudence he could, from the rage of his Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies, till his time should fully come to yield up himself to their rage; which was the reason why he, who went up now singly, without any company, when he went up to the last Passover, where he was to Suffer, went up with all imaginable boldness and alacrity; leading the way, to their amazement, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 10.32.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Then <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 11.5<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> the Jews sought him at the feast, and said, VVhere is he <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Our Saviours constant going up to the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Feasts, made the Rulers of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who sought to slay him, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.18. at <ns0:hi>the Feast of the Passover</ns0:hi> (which was but six Months before this) because he had violated the Sabbath (as they Interpreted his healing the Impotent man on that day, and bidding him take up his Bed and walk) and because he had made himself equal with God his Father, as <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5.18. seek him the first days of the Feast, speaking of him with great contempt and slight.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:343" />12 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.16. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 10.19.</ns0:note> there was much murmuring amongst the people concerning him <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Our Saviours constant attendance at these Publick Fe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stivals, did not onely create an expectation of his being there amongst his Enemies, who therefore sought him there, that they might destroy him; but amongst the ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nerality of the People, who had very different Opinions about him.</ns0:note>: For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">at. 21.46. L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ke 7.16. Chap. 6.14. Ver. 40.</ns0:note> some said, He is a good man: others said, Nay, but he de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceiveth the people <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Some having heard his Doctrine, and hear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing nothing from him but what was good and Spiritual, tending to shew them the way of Holiness, and the true Path-way to Eternal Life and Happiness, concluded that he was a good man: Others said, he was a mere Impostor, one that de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eived and cheated the more ignorant com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon People.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Howbeit, no man spake openly of him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.22. and 12.42. and 19.38.</ns0:note> for fear of the Jews <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Tho many, both of the <ns0:hi>Galileans,</ns0:hi> among whom he had conversed, and of the common People of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> had a very good Opinion of Christ, yet the Rulers of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were in such a Rage against him, that his Friends durst not freely discourse their thoughts concerning him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 ¶ Now about the midst of the feast, Jesus went up into the Temple, and taught <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">About the third or fourth day of the Feast (which continued seven days) our Lord being (as was said before) come up privately and by stealth, as it were, to <ns0:hi>Hierusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem,</ns0:hi> first appears in the Temple Preaching. What our Saviour at this time Discoursed about, the Evangelist doth not tell us; but doubtless it was the things of the Kingdom of God, which were the usual Themes or Arguments of his Discourse, as we may also understand by the latter part of it. Our Lord probably deferred his Preaching to the middle of the Feast, partly, because the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> hea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in hunting after him was now a little over; and that there might be a fuller concourse of People to hear him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And the Jews marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or <ns0:hi>learning.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> letters, having never learned <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Having never sate as a constant Disciple at the Feet of any of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Doctors, nor been Educated in their Schools of the Prophets; they wonder how he should come by such Knowledge of the Law of God, as he dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />covered in his Discourses; wherein he made it appear, that he did not onely know the letter of the Law, but the more Mysterious sense of it, the great Mysteries of the Kingdom of God.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Jesus answered them, and said <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.11. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> and 12.49. and 14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 12, 24.</ns0:note>, My Doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">My Doctrine <ns0:hi>is not mine,</ns0:hi> considering me as the Son of Man; not taught, or to be taught me by men; not learned out of Books, or by the Precepts of men; not invented by me; but it is mine as it is the Doctrine of the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> that sent me, and I and my Father both are one, and agree in one, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.7, 8 and being so, there was no such need that Christ should be <ns0:hi>Learned,</ns0:hi> in their sense, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> at the feet of their <ns0:hi>Doctors,</ns0:hi> and in their Schools. But <ns0:hi>Enthusiasts</ns0:hi> vainly argue from hence, That there is no need of Humane Learning for him who is to be a Preacher of the Gospel: For Christ was not mere man, but one in whom the fulness of the Godhead dwelt bodily. No such thing will follow from the Prophecying of <ns0:hi>Amos,</ns0:hi> who was an Herdsman, or the Apostles who were Fishermen; much less from the Preaching of Christ. We must distinguish betwixt an <ns0:hi>ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />traordinary</ns0:hi> and an <ns0:hi>ordinary</ns0:hi> Calling: And tho it be truth, That the Ministers of the Gospel Preach Doctrine which is not theirs, but his that sent them; yet it doth not follow, that they must come by the knowledge of this Doctrine in the same manner that Christ did; who was in the bosom of the Father, and knew his will, and came from him to communicate it to the World: Nor yet in the same man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner that the Prophets and the Apostles came to the know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge of it, as by Christs vocal Instruction. So also by the Influence of the Holy Spirit upon them in the days of <ns0:hi>Pentecost,</ns0:hi> which abode upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Here our Saviour seemeth to obviate an Objection which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would make, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> How they should know that the Doctrine which he Preached was the Doctrine of God? He indeed said so, but how should they have any Evidence of it? How could he make it appear to them to be of God? <ns0:hi>If any man</ns0:hi> (saith our Saviour) <ns0:hi>will do his will,</ns0:hi> &c. That is, If any man hath an Heart truly disposed to know and embrace whatsoever shall be revealed to him to be the will of God, how contrary soever it be to the Interest of his own Lust<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and ready to do it in all things; and live according to the Prescript and Revelation of it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> having a serious purpose of Heart to obey God in every thing. If he seeketh for Truth seriously, and in the fear of the Lord, laying aside all Wrath, Malice, Ha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>red, and only corrupt Passions or Affections, God will reveal the Truth to him, so as he shall know the Doctrine that is of God:</ns0:note>, or <ns0:hi>whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther</ns0:hi> I speak of my self <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">And that I do not speak of or from my self, but by Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority from my Father. Now, from hence indeed follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth, That corrupt Affections, Passions, and Prejudices<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and an ill Life, may prejudice, yea, and will prejudice men from receiving of the Free Grace of God, Spiritual Illu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minations, and the Gift of Faith: So as men that give way to such Prejudices, or nourish such Passions, or live such Lives, shall be left of God to their Native blindness, and to strong delusions, and not discern the Truth in the light that openly shineth in their Faces. But from hence it will not follow, That a Moral Life, and a study of, and a seeking after Truth, are the cause of Faith, or effective of it, with the working of our own will.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.41.</ns0:note> He that speaketh of himself, seeketh his own glory <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Here our Saviour giveth them another note, by which they might know that his Doctrine was of God, because he spake not of himself, nor sought his own Glory in what he delivered. No man doth an Action of, and from him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self, but he maketh himself the end of his Action: For to what purpose should a man devise and broach new Notions<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but for some selfish Advantage, that he may get some Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fit, or some Honour and Applause from men?</ns0:note>: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">But if a man Acts as Servant to another, and seeketh onely the Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour and Applause of another, he is true, and cannot be presumed to have spoke of, and from himself, but of and from him whose Honour and Glory he seeketh to advance; and in reason ought to be judged sincere and faithful in the execution of the Trust committed to him: And</ns0:note>, and no unrighteous<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness is in him <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">to be without fraud and deceit, having no unrighteousness in him; there being no just cause to be presumed which should move him to speak any thing that is false. Hence also may be learned a good Rule or Direction, which Divines ordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />narily make use of to help us to judge of the truth of Doctrines. Those Doctrines which most tend to the ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vancing the Honour and Glory of God, and least to the advancement of the Creature, those are most likely to be of God. And this also much tendeth to confirm the Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />putation of Holy Writ, and the Penmen of it; for it is manifest that the Penmen of it sought not their own Glory in their Writings, but the Honour and Glory of God, ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />king all shame to themselves.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Did not <ns0:note place="margin">Acts 7.35, &c<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> Moses give you the law <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> was Gods Instrument in delivering his Law to the People, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 24.3. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 33.4.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> none of you keepeth the law <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">A Law which none of them exactly kept, but daily brake; why do you (saith our Saviour) make it such a Capital Crime (suppose you were not in an <ns0:hi>Error,</ns0:hi> but I had in this one point of the Sabbath violated the Law) in me, to break the Law, that you for it would have my Blood? how cometh it to be a more hainous Offence in me to break the Law in one thing, than it is in you, who violate it in so many things? Or,</ns0:note>? VVhy <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 5.16, 18. and 10.39. and 11.53.</ns0:note> go ye about to kill me <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">do not you think it a Capital Crime maliciously to go about to destroy an Innocent Person? Is not that a greater breach, think you, of the sixth Commandment, than what I have done, is of the fourth? Supposing that had been any breach of the Law at all, which indeed it was not.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 The people answered and said <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.48, 52. and 10.20.</ns0:note>, Thou hast a devil <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had an Opinion, that whosoever was besides himself, and talked distractedly, was influenced with an <ns0:hi>Evil Spirit</ns0:hi>: So as, Thou hast a <ns0:hi>Devil,</ns0:hi> is no more than thou art Mad; unless we will take the Phrase as a mere term of Reproach, such as we ordinarily hear at this day from some men in their Passions, when they hear any speak what is false, and hath no congruity with truth, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to their apprehensions, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>aying, <ns0:hi>The Devil is in you</ns0:hi>; the former is the milder Interpretation, tho in that was sin enough, considering who it is that spake.</ns0:note>: who goeth about to kill thee <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">It is very pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bable that the common People (to whom our Saviour was now speaking) knew nothing of the design of their Ru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lers, mentioned <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.18. so spake this innocently (tho in their Passion) having no such design in their Hearts; but they ought not so peremptorily to have denied what our Saviour positively affirmed, who knew the Designs and Counsels of all mens Hearts, tho they knew them not.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Jesus answered and said unto them, I have done one work, and ye all marvel <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">By the one Miracle it is plain by what followeth, that he meaneth healing the man who lay at the Pool of <ns0:hi>Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thesda</ns0:hi>; at this, he saith, they <ns0:hi>marvelled</ns0:hi>; by which is to be understood <ns0:hi>offended</ns0:hi> (for so it is expounded by <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 23. and to this sense is our Saviours subsequent Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:344" />22 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 12.3.</ns0:note> Moses therefore <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The Particle <ns0:hi>therefore,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>for this</ns0:hi> [<ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>] maketh in this Verse a great difficulty, what the meaning of it shou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d be. The most probable a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>count of it is, that it be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />longeth to the former Verse, which should end th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s—<ns0:hi>and ye all marvel for this.</ns0:hi> This indeed maketh all plain; otherwise it is very hard to give an account what force it can have, if we consider it as a note of a cause.</ns0:note> gave unto you circum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cision <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Moses gave you Circumcision,</ns0:hi> that is, a Law about Circumcision; yet that Law had not its rise from <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>: The Law was given to your Father <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.10. long before <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> his time.</ns0:note>, (not because it is of Moses, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 12.3.</ns0:note> of the fathers) and ye on the Sabbath-day circumcise a man <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">In obedience to that Law, you Circum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cise a <ns0:hi>Male Child,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Proselyte,</ns0:hi> that is, a man grown, on the Sabbath-day.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 If a man on the Sabbath-day receive Cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumcision, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>without breaking the Law of</ns0:hi> Moses.</ns0:note> that the law of Moses should not be broken <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The strength of this whole Argument seemeth to be this. If a Ritual Law (such was that for observation of the Sabbath, given in Mount <ns0:hi>Sinai, Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.) may give place to another <ns0:hi>Ritual Law</ns0:hi> which is ancienter (such was that of Circumcision, given to <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> long before) much more ought it to give place to a Law of Nature wrote in every mans Heart, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That it is our Duty to help those that are in great degrees of Misery and Affliction; which is what I paid Obedience to in Curing the Impotent man that lay at the Pool of <ns0:hi>Bethesda.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Do you yield this in your daily practice, that a man may be Circumcised, yea, and ought to be Circumcised on the eight day, tho it happeneth to be the Sabbath-day; and not to do it, were a violation of the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> about Circumcision, which was a Law given you by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> tho before him, to <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> also?</ns0:note>, are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the Sabbath-day <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">What reason then have you to be Angry with me, who on the Sabbath-day have onely healed a man, and made him <ns0:hi>every whit whole</ns0:hi>: That is (as some think) I have not onely Cured him as to his Body, but as to his Soul, (but that hardly seemeth probable; for if it were so, the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> could have no Evidence of the Spiritual Cure.) Others therefore think that the term <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, signifieth no more than <ns0:hi>perfectly,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>compleatly</ns0:hi> whole, as to his Body.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 1.16. Prov. 24.23.</ns0:note> Judge not according to the appearance <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Do not Judge Persons, and condemn me for what I have done, merely out of your Hatred, Prejudice, and Malice against me. Or do not judge according to the first appearance of this Fact. It looketh to you as a violation of the Sabbath; it is not indeed so, but the performance of a Duty greater than that of Sanctifying the Sabbath is.</ns0:note>, but judge righteous judgment <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Judge Righteously, and do not condemn in me what you your selves do in other causes, because of your hatred to, and prejudice against me; nor condemn an Action which is in it self a Righteous Action, and not deserving Condem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Then said some of them of Jerusalem, Is not this he whom they seek to kill <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Those who here speak, are said to be of <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> (probably Citizens) who knew more of the Designs and Counsels of the Chief Priests and Elders, than those who said before, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>Thou hast a Devil: who seeketh to kill thee?</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 But lo, he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing unto him <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The first search being over, it is probable that the Ru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lers had not heard that Christ was come up to the Feast; this made the People think,</ns0:note>: Do the rulers know indeed that this is the very Christ <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That they had some know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge that he was the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi>; otherwise they would have taken some course to have restrained his so free and open Discoursing: But we shall in the latter part of this Chap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter find that they were mistaken; for as soon as they heard where he was, and what he was doing, they used all means they could to Apprehend him.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 13.55. Mark 6.3. Luke 4.22.</ns0:note> Howbeit we know this man whence he is <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">We know he is of <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> and that <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> is his <ns0:hi>re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />puted Father.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: but when Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">They also knew whence the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> was to come; That he was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of the <ns0:hi>Family of David,</ns0:hi> of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iuda,</ns0:hi> of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Town of <ns0:hi>Bethlehem.</ns0:hi> The Chief Priests and Scribes <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> to that purpose, without the least hesitation, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 2.6. but they had no Revelation to guide them to know of what particular Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mily he should be; thus this Verse is easily reconciled to <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 42, Others think, that they speak of the second ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifestation of Christ. They had a Tradition, which was bottomed on Holy Writ, That he was to come out of <ns0:hi>Beth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lehem</ns0:hi>: But then they had another Tradition; That he should be taken away from thence, and hidden for some Years, and then again appear as a Person unknown whence he came. Which Opinion, say some, was bottomed on the Revelations of the Old Testament concerning a double Regeneration of Christ, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.8. <ns0:hi>Who shall declare his Generation? Micah</ns0:hi> 5.2. The one of which is to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood of his <ns0:hi>Eternal Generation,</ns0:hi> which none can de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clare. The other, as to the <ns0:hi>Generation of his Humane Nature.</ns0:hi> But the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> not understanding that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was to be <ns0:hi>God-man,</ns0:hi> understood both of his Humane Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture; which made them fancy, that tho he was to be Born at <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> according to <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 5.2. yet he was to be carried away for some Years some whither; so as when he came to appear to the World, none should know whence he came; but he should appear as a man dropped down from Heaven Now Christ having been offered in the Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple at his Mothers Purification, went back again with his Parents, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 2.39. came to <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> and ordinarily went up to <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi>; there he was found Disputing with the Doctors, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 46. And at last, we find him resting with his Parents at <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>being subject to them</ns0:hi>; after which we read no more of him, till he came to <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> to be Baptized; so as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had known and observed the whole course of Christs Life.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Then cried Jesus in the Temple as he taught, saying, Ye both know me, and ye know whence I am <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">You might have known me by the Doctrine which I have taught, and the Miracles which I have wrought among you<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and you had known me, if you had not shut your Eyes against the Light, which shone in your Face. Or you say, and think that you know me; others think that it is an <ns0:hi>Irony,</ns0:hi> or as a Question, Do you know me so well?</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.43. and 8.42.</ns0:note> I am not come of my self, but he that sent me <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.32. and 8.26.</ns0:note> is true, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. and 8.55.</ns0:note> whom ye know not <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">If you did, you would know that I came not of my self, but was sent by my Father; and he that sent me is Truth it self; but you know not the Father, and therefore cannot know me as indeed I am.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> I know him <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I know him, so as no man else knoweth him, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 11.27. I know his Essence, his Will, his Counsels, his Laws,</ns0:note>, for I am from him <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">for I am from him by an Eternal Generation, his onely begotten Son;</ns0:note>, and he hath sent me <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">and I am sent by him, as the Mediator and Saviour of the World, to declare, and to execute his Will and Pleasure, as to mans Salvation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Then <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 11.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Luke 19.47. and 20.19. Chap. 8.37.</ns0:note> they sought to take him <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">By this time the News was come to the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim,</ns0:hi> the great Court of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> to whom belonged the cognisance of Church-Affairs, <ns0:hi>False Prophets, Blasphemy, Violation of the Sabbath,</ns0:hi> &c. they took Counsel, and used endeavours to Apprehend him; or it may be, some of the ruder sort of People that were his Enemies used some such endea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vours, but not with any effect; for by the mighty Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence of God, who had set the time when Christ should suffer; till that hour was come, mentioned also <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 8.20. and 12.23. there was such a restraint upon the rage of the <ns0:hi>Rabble</ns0:hi>; yea (as we shall hereafter hear) the Spirits of the Officers, who were sent from the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim</ns0:hi> to Apprehend him, that they had no power to lay hold upon him. Men shall do us no hurt, till Gods time comes. <ns0:hi>A Sparrow falls not to the ground without the will of our Father.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 44.</ns0:note> no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come <ns0:hi>t.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> many of the people believed on him <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Not as the true <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi>; for the next words let us know, they did not believe him to be the Christ, but look'd for him to come; but they gave Credit to him, as a great <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> sent from God: And</ns0:note>, and said, VVhen Christ cometh, will he do mo mira<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>les than these which this <ns0:hi>man</ns0:hi> hath done <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">doubted whether the Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racles which he wrought, were not as many, and as great as ever the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> would do when he came. For tho <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> reports but a few Miracles wrought by Christ, yet they were such as required a Divine Power to produce; such as turning the Water into Wine, multiplying the Loaves, raising <ns0:hi>Lazarus</ns0:hi> from the dead, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> And <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 20.30. and 21.25. That he did many more works than he hath Recorded in this Book; and many more are Recorded by the other three <ns0:hi>Evangelists.</ns0:hi> From hence may be observed the falshood of the later <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who deny that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> is to work any Miracles; for it is apparent from hence, that they had in our Saviours time a general expectation of great Miracles should be done by the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; and their expectation was truly founded upon <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 35.5, 6. as appeareth by <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 11.5.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:344" />32 ¶ The Pharisees heard that the people mur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mured <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Murmured</ns0:hi> here is taken in a different sense from what it was before, and signifieth as much as whispered, or <ns0:hi>talked privately</ns0:hi> among themselves.</ns0:note> such things concerning him: and the Pharisees, and the chief Priests sent officers to take him <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The Chief Priests, who were afraid that their Honour would abate amongst the People; and the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> who were afraid the Cre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dit of their Traditions would be lost, if they suffered him to go on; and being more especially troubled for the Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racles which he daily wrought, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.47. They send <ns0:hi>Messengers</ns0:hi> from their great Court (kept at <ns0:hi>Hierusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem</ns0:hi>) to Apprehend him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Then said Jesus unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.16.</ns0:note> Yet a little while I am with you, and <ns0:hi>then</ns0:hi> I go to him that sent me <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Whether Christ spake these words to the Officers sent to Apprehend him, or to the people in the Temple, is not much material to be known: He by them plainly declareth, that all their endeavours against him were vain and foolish; for he should yet live with them six Months (this was in <ns0:hi>September</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>October,</ns0:hi> he dyed at the next Passover, which was about six Months after this) and then he should <ns0:hi>go</ns0:hi> and willingly lay down his Life for the sins of the World, rise again from the dead, and ascend unto his Father who sent him into the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.21.</ns0:note> Ye shall seek me, and shall not find <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Some think the meaning is, <ns0:hi>You shall seek me,</ns0:hi> to ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ecute your malice upon me, but to no purpose, for you shall not find me. Or, you shall seek me to destroy me in my Church, and to root out my Name, but to no purpose. But the most probable sense is this; you wicked <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> that now contemn the means of Grace by me offered to you, shall one day be in distress and calamity enough; and when you are so, then you will wish I were again amongst you; but I shall be Ascended to my Father;</ns0:note>: and where I am, <ns0:hi>thither</ns0:hi> ye cannot come <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">and as deaf to your Prayers, as above the reach of your malice. There is much the same thing said in <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 23.39. That he here speaketh of his Ascension is plain from <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 13.33. He speaketh of Heaven as a place where he was at that time, for so he was as to his Divine Nature. It is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, whither I go; which makes some think, it should not here be <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, but <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>vado.</ns0:hi> But others reject it, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause it is a Poetical word, hardly used in the New Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him <ns0:hi>c</ns0:hi>? will he go unto the dispersed among the <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> Greeks.</ns0:note> Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">In the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>Will he go into the dispersion of the Grecians.</ns0:hi> There were two most Famous dispersions, of which we read in story. The first was of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> of which we read in Sacred History, in the Captivities of <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> (whither the Ten Tribes were carried, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 17.6.) and <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> whither the two Tribes were carried, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 17.25. And that of the <ns0:hi>Gre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cians</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Macedonians</ns0:hi>; when also many of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were dispersed by <ns0:hi>Alexander</ns0:hi> the Great, and his Successors. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> directeth his Epistle to the <ns0:hi>Strangers</ns0:hi> scattered throughout <ns0:hi>Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>By<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thynia,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.1. And <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> directs his Epistle to the <ns0:hi>Twelve Tribes scattered abroad.</ns0:hi> They fancy that our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour would go into some of these places, and Preach; by which means the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> would be taught the Myste<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ries of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Religion, which was what above all things they were impatient of hearing; and yet had rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son from the Prophecies of the Old Testament, to fear, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> their own Rejection, and the receiving in of the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles,</ns0:hi> which afterward came to pass, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 11.15.</ns0:note>?<ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> not at all believing the Divine Nature of Christ, notwithstanding all that Christ had said, and all the Miracles he had wrought, are at a mighty loss to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clude what our Saviour spake of, and whither he would go; they thought he could go no where in the Land of <ns0:hi>Iewry,</ns0:hi> but they should hear of him, and be able to come where he was; they conclude therefore that he would go into some <ns0:hi>Pagan</ns0:hi> Countrey.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 VVhat <ns0:hi>manner of</ns0:hi> saying is this that he said, Ye shall seek me, and shall not find <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi>: and where I am, <ns0:hi>thither</ns0:hi> ye cannot come <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This saying stuck in their Stomacks, and they knew not what sense to put upon it; owning nothing of the Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Nature of Christ.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 23.36.</ns0:note> In the last day, that great <ns0:hi>day</ns0:hi> of the feast <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Our Saviour thinketh not fit to take any notice of their guess, whither he would go, nor replyeth any thing to it. The <ns0:hi>Feast of Tabernacles</ns0:hi> was to hold seven days, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 23.34. in which they were to offer up Burnt-Offerings, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 36. The <ns0:hi>Eight day</ns0:hi> was to be kept as a Sabbath; there was in it to be an <ns0:hi>Holy Convocation,</ns0:hi> no Servile Labour was to be done. Christ on that day Discoursed again to the People, crying aloud, and publickly,</ns0:note>, Jesus stood and cryed, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.35. Rev. 22.17.</ns0:note> If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>If any man be a thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.</ns0:hi> That is, if any man stand in need of any Spiritual Good, Righteousness, Strength, Comfort, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> it is to be found in me; let him come to me, by Faith acknowledging, receiving, and embracing me, as the Mediator and Saviour of the World, and he shall have from me whatsoever Spiritual Influence of Grace he stands in need of. Those who remember what our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour told the Woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria, Chap.</ns0:hi> 4.10, 14. where he compared himself to <ns0:hi>Living water,</ns0:hi> will easily under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand this the sense of these words: The Condition on our parts is expressed under the notion of <ns0:hi>Thirsting</ns0:hi>; which we know is the Natural Appetite, craving some liquid thing to refresh the man under his Drought; and it is expressive of an exceeding great Passion, and so made use of both in the Old Testament and the New, to signifie a Souls passionate desire of Spiritual things, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 55.1. <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 5.6.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 18.15.</ns0:note> He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">We have had frequent occasion to open the term of <ns0:hi>believing on Christ</ns0:hi>: It may be doubted, whether those words (<ns0:hi>as the Scripture hath said</ns0:hi>) be to be referred to the first or latter part of the Text. If to the former, they are words expressive of that Faith to which the following Promise is made, which is not any assent, or slightly credit given to the word; but such a Faith as the Scripture hath spoken of; as that Faith which is justifying and saving.</ns0:note>, out <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 44.3.</ns0:note> of his belly shall flow rivers of living water <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The general sense of the Promises, That his Soul shall abound with all saving and comfortable Influences of sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving Grace. The <ns0:hi>Belly</ns0:hi> signifieth the Heart (that part of man, which is called the Heart, being in the Belly.) So <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 15.35. Psal. 40.8. the <ns0:hi>flowing of Rivers of water,</ns0:hi> sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth the plenty of Spiritual Influences with which Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lievers shall be supplied; whether Joy, Knowledge, Spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual Gifts, or Graces. If any ask, where the Scripture speaketh this? I Answer, in all those Promises we meet with in the Old Testament, about pouring out the Spirit.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 (<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joel 2.28. Acts 2.17.</ns0:note> But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him, should receive <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">For the Evangelist tells us, that this referred to the Spirit, which Believers were to receive after that Christ should be Ascended into Heaven. Those Scriptures, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 49.10. and 58.11. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 14.8. seem, among others, to be referred to in this Promise of our Saviour.</ns0:note>: for the holy Ghost was not yet <ns0:hi>given,</ns0:hi> because that Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus was not yet glorified <ns0:hi>l.</ns0:hi>)</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 ¶ Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the <ns0:note place="margin">Chap. 6.14.</ns0:note> Prophet <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 18.15. Some think that the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> expected an eminent Prophet besides <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> to come before the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.21. would incline us to think so. But others say, it cannot be proved from their Writers, that they had any expectations of any but <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi> But the words may be read as well, This is <ns0:hi>a Prophet,</ns0:hi> as this is <ns0:hi>the Prophet</ns0:hi>; and I think that is the true sense of them. A Prophet had now for more than four hundred years been a great Rarity amongst them; they having had none but <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist</ns0:hi> who had such a Repute.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 Others said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.42.</ns0:note> This is the Christ. But some said, Shall Christ come <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.46. Ver. 52.</ns0:note> out of Galilee <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The People were divided in their Opinions about Christ. Some of them were very well inclined to believe that he was the Promised <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; but they stumbled at the Countrey where alone they took notice of him. For tho he came not out of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> but was Born in <ns0:hi>Bethle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hem, Luke</ns0:hi> 2.4. according to the Prophecy of him, <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 5.2. Sutable to which was their Tradition, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 2.5. Yet they had seen nothing of this, tho possibly they had heard some relation of it, it being Two and Thirty years since his Birth: But he was ordinarily called <ns0:hi>Iesus of Nazareth,</ns0:hi> and of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> there he had lived, and been Educated; so as they knew no better probably than that he came out of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> which was contrary to the Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 5.2.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 2.5. Luke 2.4.</ns0:note> Hath not the scripture said, That Christ cometh of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The Scriptures of the Old Testament had both de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scribed the Family from whence the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was to arise, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the Family of <ns0:hi>David, Psal.</ns0:hi> 132.11. and the Town, which was <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> Micah 5.2. which was <ns0:hi>Davids</ns0:hi> Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers Town, where he lived also, till God called him out to the Kingdom, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 17.15. and 20.6.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:345" />43 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.16. and 10.19.</ns0:note> So there was a division among the people because of him <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">A Division as to their Opinions about him, as was be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore expressed.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 30.</ns0:note> some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">There were some that had an ill Opinion of Christ, and put on the Officers that came for the purpose to Ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehend him; but there was none so hardy as to do it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 ¶ Then came the officers to the chief Priests and Pharisees, and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Probably the Officers, Christ being amongst a multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude of the People that had an high Opinion of him, durst not adventure to Apprehend him: Some of them, as ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peareth from what follows, were astonished at his Doctrine; all of them agreed to return to their Masters without him; at which they are angry, and ask them, how it came to pass, that they did not execute their Commands, in bring<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Christ before them as a Malefactor, to answer what they should lay to his Charge.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 The officers answered, Never man spake like this man <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">With so much Authority, Evidence of truth, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Yet they did not cordially believe in Christ; being under the power of Carnal and Worldly Affections, which onely supernatural Special Grace could subdue. These were some of those, in whom the Prophecy of Christ, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 11.4. was to be fulfilled.—<ns0:hi>He shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.</ns0:hi> The word of the Lord doth often restrain, astonish, and amaze those on whom it hath no powerful effect to Eternal Life and Salvation. So it was with these poor Officers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">You, who have us not onely for your Masters, whose Commands you ought not to dispute, but to execute; but for your Teachers also, from whom you might have learn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed better Doctrine; are you <ns0:hi>seduced?</ns0:hi> For so wicked men count all who embrace not their Notions, and follow not their ways.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 12.42. Acts 6.7. 1 Cor. 1.20. and 2.8.</ns0:note> Have any of the rulers, or of the Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees believed on him <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">You ought to be ruled by us, and guided by us, who are your Rulers, and your Teachers, (so early did the Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine of <ns0:hi>implicite Faith</ns0:hi> and Obedience creep into the World) which is indeed to suppose an Infallibility in Teach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers and Rulers, to whom indeed we owe all imaginable Reverence; but we must live by our own Faith: And tho the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were bound up, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 17.10, 11. to <ns0:hi>do according to the sentiments</ns0:hi> that the Priests and <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> should shew them; yet <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. <ns0:hi>it must be the sentence of the Law,</ns0:hi> and it was in Civil matters, as appeareth by <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 8. Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />troversies between <ns0:hi>Blood</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Blood, Plea</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Plea, Stroak</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Stroak.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 But this people who knoweth not the Law are cursed <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Out of the great Pride of their Hearts they vilifie the people, as not Learned in the Law, and so were cursed, contemptible, and not to be regarded, as to their judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment and sentiments.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>to him.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Jesus by night, being one of them) <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Of <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi> we read, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.2. and of his com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing by Night to Jesus. He now being one of this great Court, stands up to speak for Christ, yet faintly, or at least wonderfully prudently, and warily. He saith no more for him than he ought to have spoken for the greatest Male<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />factor, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 1.17. and 17.8, &c. and 19.15.</ns0:note> Doth our law judge any man before it hear him, and know what he doeth <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">That no Law of God or Nature Condemneth any man before they had heard him speak, or had what he did de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed by Witnesses before them, that they might know what he did.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Not that they thought <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Galilean</ns0:hi>; they knew him well enough; but they take up this as a term of Reproach against him, for that he would offer to speak one word (tho never so just) on the behalf of one against whom they had such a perfect hatred.</ns0:note>? Search, and look: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 4.15. Chap. 1.46.</ns0:note> out of Galilee ariseth no prophet <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Search, say they, the Scriptures, and look if ever there came a Prophet out of <ns0:hi>Galilee.</ns0:hi> Suppose this had been truth; yet 1. What did this concern our Saviour? who was not Born in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> but in <ns0:hi>Iuda</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> the City of <ns0:hi>David, Luke</ns0:hi> 24. 2. Could not God when he pleased influence one of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> with the Spirit of Prophecy? But 3. Neither was it true; for <ns0:hi>Nahum</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ionah</ns0:hi> were both <ns0:hi>Galileans,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 14.25. compared with <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 19.13. (for the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Zebulon</ns0:hi> had their Lot in <ns0:hi>Galilee) Isaiah</ns0:hi> 9.1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 And every man went unto his own house <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">As little as <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi> said for Christ, it put a stop to their further proceedings against Christ at present: Some think that the party of the <ns0:hi>Sadduces</ns0:hi> in the Council, who valued not the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> Rites and Traditions, took part with <ns0:hi>Nicodemus</ns0:hi>; so as by the over-ruling hand of God Christ at this time escaped their wicked Counsels against him. So much is certain; but what parties in the Council concurred in it, is uncertain.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
